races.title: State House, District 36
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Julie von Haefen
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 36 (southern Wake County) since 2019. Attorney who practiced over 10 years in criminal, medical malpractice defense, municipal and education law. Former Wake County PTA Council president, Guardian ad Litem and substitute teacher.

controversies.text: On June 14, 2025, von Haefen shared a No Kings rally video that included a protester's sign showing a guillotine and a beheaded Trump figure. She removed the image, said she condemns political violence, and apologized on the House floor on June 17. She also deleted her X account, which one outlet said may breach records laws.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina endorsed her in 2026 (listed by Ballotpedia).
Humane World Action Fund endorsed her in 2026 (listed by Ballotpedia).

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised; her campaign site mentions a Cincinnati hometown football team but does not state a birthplace. We found no record of her stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, policing, or gun laws. We also found no news reporting on the 2025 social media controversy beyond a Wikipedia summary. The campaign site's issues page on abortion was cut off, so only the portion we read is reported.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she and her husband moved to Apex and District 36 in 2005, about 21 years ago as an adult; her birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2019 (Appropriations and Finance among her committee assignments), after more than 10 years practicing law in criminal, medical malpractice defense, municipal and education law.
qual.why: Several terms of legislative service, including budget-writing committee work, plus a legal career put her in the high band. Committee seats and PTA or volunteer roles were not counted.
qual.label: Several terms of legislative service, including budget-writing committee work, plus a legal career put her in the high band. Committee seats and PTA or volunteer roles were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Says abortion is healthcare, and promises to fight legislation such as a 13-week abortion ban (HB 28) and other abortion restrictions.

prio.label: Matches 0 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 0 only promised (needs 2 to score)

cands.name: Mary Insprucker
cands.bio: Republican candidate for NC House District 36 in 2026. Describes herself as a former nonprofit regional director, consultant to the Town of Cary, Wake County substitute teacher, American Red Cross board member, and journalist and media professional. Has not held elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no birthplace, upbringing or move-in date for her, so her ties to North Carolina are not scored. We could not independently confirm her job history, including the Midwest nonprofit director role, the Town of Cary consulting work and the awards. These come from her own campaign site. We found no record of her taking action on any platform topic, only her stated positions. We found nothing on her views on data centers, development and growth, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or donor money. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her, and her site's endorsements page was not in the material we had. The last part of her campaign priorities page (the conservation and transportation section) was cut off, so anything after "Smarter transportation planni" was not read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Self-described former Regional Director of a large Midwest nonprofit, consultant to the Town of Cary, Wake County substitute teacher, and award-winning writer and media professional. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: She has management and government-consulting work but no legislative service and no budget or law career that the pages document. Board seats and volunteer roles are not counted. The job history comes from her own descriptions and has not been independently verified.
qual.label: She has management and government-consulting work but no legislative service and no budget or law career that the pages document. Board seats and volunteer roles are not counted. The job history comes from her own descriptions and has not been independently verified.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says she wants "tax reduction guardrails" on property taxes, including caps on reevaluation increases and limits on tax levies. She supports a constitutional amendment (HB 1089) to limit growth in local property-tax levies and criticizes county overspending. She does not call for eliminating homestead taxes.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she supports higher teacher pay and Opportunity Scholarships, and that it is a parent's right to choose the best school for their child.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she will support school resource officers, bring funding home for first responders and a robust police force, and advocate for cash bail and mental health evaluations for defendants with a violent history.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised
